phonemes.desc: Initial sound of Śiva, as attested in the sanskrit tradition.
Subsequent syllables preserve the name's inherited shape.

pronunciation.note: Śiva is Tier 2 because its Unicode restoration preserves the orthographic signature appropriate to the sanskrit tradition.

domains.title: Destruction, Transformation, Dance
domains.subtitle: The domain of Śiva
domains.lead: In the sanskrit tradition, Śiva governed destruction, transformation, dance. The name encodes a sphere of power that shaped ritual, narrative, and social order.

cards.title: Primary Sphere
cards.body: Śiva is principally associated with destruction, transformation, dance.

cards.title: Cultural Role
cards.body: Worshippers approached Śiva through cult, myth, and the material culture of the sanskrit world.

symbols.name: Cult site
symbols.meaning: Sanctuary or holy place where Śiva was honoured

symbols.name: Ritual object
symbols.meaning: Material focus of devotion for Śiva

mythology.lead: The myths of Śiva preserve the name's power and personality across generations of retelling.

myths.title: The story of Śiva
myths.text: Śiva appears in sanskrit tradition as a figure whose domain over destruction, transformation, dance shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Śiva's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Śiva in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Śiva carries within it a sanskrit understanding of auspicious, kind (from शिव). Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
